words.gloss: bilva (Aegle marmelos, bael; standard) and others
bṛhatī (the pair bṛhatī, Solanum indicum, and kaṇṭakārī, Solanum virginianum; standard), of the two

hindi: बिल्व यानी बेल आदि के अथवा दोनों बृहतियों यानी बड़ी कटेरी और छोटी कटेरी के काढ़े से, बराबर मात्रा में, एक-एक करके।
english: With a decoction of bilva (bael) and the others, or of the two bṛhatī (the large and the small thorny nightshade), in equal measure, each one separately,
notes: GROUPING: each unit is one 16-syllable half-verse line; this sentence runs on into 113. kvāthena = decoction (glossary). bṛhatyoḥ is dual: the two bṛhatī, taken in the standard way as bṛhatī (Solanum indicum) and kaṇṭakārī (Solanum virginianum, also called S. xanthocarpum): standard pair, species names probable.

words.gloss: milk (latex) of sudhā (Euphorbia neriifolia, spurge; synonym snuhī/snuk; standard)

hindi: सुधा यानी थूहर के दूध को मिलाकर फिर अंगारों पर सुखाए।
english: Having mixed in the milk of sudhā (spurge), one should then dry it on embers.
notes: GROUPING: continues 112 (the decoction of 112 is the understood thing mixed). kṣīra rendered literally as milk (it may mean a sap); not decided. The text prints anusvāra for the class nasal (aṃgāra for aṅgāra): ordinary print spelling, not flagged. Enrichment: sudhā = snuhī/snuk, Euphorbia neriifolia (standard); Hindi थूहर or सेंहुड़. The kṣīra of this plant is its white latex (probable); the translation keeps 'milk'.

words.gloss: mastu (curd whey), urine, surā (grain-based spirituous drink), and so on

hindi: गोली बनाकर मस्तु यानी दही का पानी, मूत्र, सुरा यानी अनाज की बनी मदिरा आदि के साथ पिए।
english: Having made it into a pill, one should drink it with mastu (curd whey), urine, surā (a grain-based spirituous drink) and the like.
notes: GROUPING: continues 112-113 (the dried mass becomes the pill). mastu = a liquid from curds (literal sense kept as mastu). Word order is pibet before kṛtvā; translated in natural order.

words.gloss: trivṛt (Operculina turpethum, turpeth; standard) and others
varā (drug name; disputed, often read as triphalā; lit. excellent)
together with sātalā (drug name; identity disputed)

hindi: त्रिवृत् यानी निशोथ आदि नौ को, वरा, स्वर्णक्षीरी यानी संभवतः सत्यानाशी और सातला के सहित,
english: The nine beginning with trivṛt (turpeth), varā and svarṇakṣīrī (probably prickly poppy), together with sātalā,

text_flags.why: stray anusvāra and a doubled n; the two words are joined: trivṛta-ādīn nava (possible)

notes: GROUPING: the sentence runs through 116 (object here; verb pibet in 116). nava taken as nine; 'new' is a possible alternative. varā: disputed (often triphalā; not decided). svarṇakṣīrī: probably Argemone mexicana (probable). sātalā: disputed, no identification adopted. The nine drugs of the trivṛt group are not listed here.

words.gloss: steeped in (lit. drunk) milk (latex) of snuk (= sudhā, Euphorbia neriifolia; see 113)

hindi: उन्हें, जो सात दिन तक स्नुक् यानी थूहर का दूध पिए हुए हों, रस अथवा घी के साथ पिए।
english: Those that have drunk snuk milk (spurge latex) for seven days, one should drink with juice or with ghee.
notes: GROUPING: completes the sentence begun in 115. pītān is literally 'drunk'; read as having absorbed the milk (steeped). rasa taken as 'juice'; 'taste' is a less likely alternative. snuk = snuhī, the plant of 113 (standard). saptāham could also be construed with pibet (drink for seven days) instead of with pītān.

hindi: उसी प्रकार वया, उपोत्तमा, निकुम्भ, कुम्भ आदि को गुड़ के जल के साथ।
english: Likewise vayā(?), upottamā(?), nikumbha(?), kumbha and the others, with jaggery water.

text_flags.why: possible: 17 syllables for a 16-syllable line ('po' seems extra) and kuṃbhāni is probably nikuṃbhān (cf. nikuṃbha-kuṃbha in 120); not certain

notes: The reading of the first token is doubtful, so the drug names are tentative. tadvat refers back to the week-long steeping in snuk milk (115-116). Low confidence. GROUPING: this half-verse has no verb of its own; with 'tadvat' it probably continues the construction of 116 (pibet), possibly of adyāt in 118. Not decided.

words.gloss: with decoction of śyāmā and trivṛt (turpeth, see 115), snuk milk (latex), ghee and phāṇita (treacle, thickened sugarcane juice)

hindi: श्यामा और त्रिवृत् के काढ़े, स्नुक् के दूध, घृत और फाणित यानी राब के साथ खाए।
english: One should eat it with a decoction of śyāmā and trivṛt, snuk milk, ghee and phāṇita (treacle).

text_flags.why: kātha should be kvātha (decoction); a scan slip (same in 140)

notes: Whether 'decoction' governs only śyāmā-trivṛt or the whole list is not certain; read as governing śyāmā-trivṛt. The object of adyāt is not stated. Enrichment: śyāmā is disputed (in Caraka often the black kind of trivṛt, so śyāmā-trivṛt may be one drug; not decided). phāṇita = thickened sugarcane juice (standard); Hindi राब.

words.gloss: with kāsāri (drug name, unidentified) juice, thin pulse soup (yūṣa), and the like

hindi: अथवा कासारि के रस, यूष यानी दाल का पतला रस आदि से युक्त स्नुक् का दूध पिए।
english: Or one should drink snuk milk combined with the juice of kāsāri, broth and the like.
notes: kāsāri is kept as a drug name; it is kept as a drug name and not analysed. yūṣa = a broth. The compound could also be read 'juice of kāsāri, broth, etc.' (as done) or 'kāsāri-juice-broth'. Enrichment: kāsāri is unidentified. yūṣa = a thin strained soup, usually of pulses (standard).

words.gloss: powder of nikumbha, kumbha (both unidentified), śyāmā (disputed), arka (Calotropis procera or C. gigantea, madar; standard), śaṅkhinī (disputed) and samalā (unidentified)

hindi: निकुम्भ, कुम्भ, श्यामा, अर्क यानी आक, शंखिनी और समला का चूर्ण,
english: The powder of nikumbha, kumbha, śyāmā, arka (swallow-wort), śaṅkhinī and samalā,

text_flags.why: possible: śyābhā is not a known drug name; śyāmā (cf. 118) is probable

notes: GROUPING: the sentence continues through 121 (the powder is kept in urine and in the heat). arka kept as a drug name (it also means 'sun'). rajas = powder (also 'dust').

hindi: रात में मूत्र में और दिन में गर्मी में सात दिन तक रखे; इस प्रकार।
english: At night in urine, by day in the heat, for seven days one should keep it; thus.

text_flags.why: stray anusvāra; the locative is gharme

notes: GROUPING: completes the sentence of 120. gharma = heat (often the sun's heat); rendered 'heat'. The object is the powder of 120.
lines_deva: रात्रौ मूत्रे दिवा घर्में सप्ताहं स्थापयेदिति
lines_iast: rātrau mūtre divā gharmeṃ saptāhaṃ sthāpayediti

hindi: स्नुक् के दूध में भी; फिर उससे चूर्ण छिड़की हुई माला या वस्त्र,
english: Also in snuk milk; then a garland or cloth sprinkled with that (powder),
notes: GROUPING: continues in 123 (the garland or cloth is smelled / worn). The meaning of 'api' (also in snuk milk) is unclear: perhaps the powder is also steeped in snuk milk. 'garland or cloth': both are neuter and both go with avacūrṇitam.

hindi: सूँघे; और ओढ़े हुए मृदु कोष्ठ वाला पुरुष विरेचित होता है।
english: One should smell it, and one who covers oneself with it, being of soft bowel (koṣṭha), is purged.
notes: GROUPING: completes the sentence begun in 122. The subject of ājighret and prāvṛṇānaḥ is read as the same person; mṛdu-koṣṭha could also be read with ājighret. Enrichment: mṛdu-koṣṭha = one with a 'soft' bowel, i.e. a person whose bowel is easily purged (standard classification mṛdu / madhya / krūra koṣṭha); viricyate = undergoes purgation (virecana).

words.gloss: of śaṅkhinī (drug name; identity disputed, none adopted)

hindi: शंखिनी का फल, जो बहुत सूखा न हो, लेना चाहिए, भूसी से रहित किया हुआ।
english: The fruit of śaṅkhinī, not too dry, should be taken, freed from its husk.

text_flags.why: possible: genitive expected (visarga missing); the instrumental reading does not fit

notes: nistupī- is probably nistuṣī- (niḥ + tuṣa, 'without husk'; possible print or scan slip, not in text_flags); the husk sense is kept literal. Enrichment: śaṅkhinī is disputed (several different plants are given under this name); no identification is adopted here.

words.gloss: sharp (tīkṣṇa) and vikāṣin (loosening the bonds of the tissues)

hindi: तथा समला की जड़; वे दोनों तो तीक्ष्ण और विकाषी यानी धातुओं के बन्धन को ढीला करने वाले हैं।
english: And also the root of samalā; those two, however, are sharp and vikāṣin (loosening the bonds of the tissues).

text_flags.why: possible: ṣ for ś; vikāśin/vikāsin is the usual technical word (also printed vikāṣi in 133, vikāṣitā in 136)

notes: vikāṣin (classical vikāśin) is a technical quality; in the standard definition it loosens the bonds of the tissues (dhātu); the text here does not define it; 'te' refers to the fruit of śaṅkhinī and the root of samalā.

words.gloss: belly (udara), poison (gara, compound poison), swelling (śvayathu, oedema), and so on

hindi: कफ के रोगों में, उदर में, गर यानी कृत्रिम विष में, शोथ आदि में प्रयोग करे।
english: In Kapha-afflictions, udara, gara (compound poison), swelling (oedema) and the like, one should prescribe it.

text_flags.why: the compound śleṣmāmaya-udara-... is wrongly divided by a space

notes: Read as one compound śleṣma-āmaya-udara-gara-śvayathu-ādiṣu. udara = belly (the named disorder of the belly); gara = poison. The object of kalpayet is the preparation of 125. Enrichment: gara = poison made by combining substances (kṛtrima viṣa; standard). In this list udara most probably names the disease udara (enlargement of the belly, ascites-type); the translation keeps 'belly' (earlier sense decision).

words.gloss: an akṣa in measure (one akṣa = one karṣa, about 10 to 12 g in the usual tables)
combined with madirā (spirituous drink) and salt

hindi: उन दोनों का अक्ष भर पिण्ड, मदिरा और नमक से युक्त,
english: A lump of the two, an akṣa in measure, combined with madirā and salt,
notes: akṣa = a unit of measure. The sentence continues into 128. 'tayoḥ' = of the fruit and the root of 124-125. Enrichment: akṣa = karṣa in the standard weight tables (about 10 to 12 g depending on the table); probable. madirā = a strong spirituous drink.

words.gloss: in heart-disease (lit. disease of the heart)
in the gulma (abdominal lump) of that

hindi: वात और कफ से उत्पन्न हृदय के रोग में और उसके गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ में भी प्रयोग करे।
english: One should apply it in heart-disease born of Vāta and Kapha, and also in its gulma (abdominal lump).
notes: tad-gulma is ambiguous ('gulma of that', i.e. of the heart-disease, or 'that gulma'). gulma is kept (a lump or mass). hṛdroga is heart disease (disorders of the heart, with pain in the chest region); gulma is a lump or mass felt in the belly (standard).

words.gloss: of paste of tila (sesame, Sesamum indicum; standard)

hindi: शंखिनी के चूर्ण के दो भाग और तिल के कल्क का एक और भाग,
english: Two portions of śaṅkhinī powder, and one more of tila (sesame) paste,
notes: 'aparaḥ' read as 'one other (portion)'. Sentence continues in 130 (the oil of that). kalka = paste.

words.gloss: with decoction of harītakī (Terminalia chebula, chebulic myrobalan; standard)

hindi: हरीतकी यानी हरड़ के काढ़े के साथ उसका तेल, निचोड़ा हुआ, पिए।
english: The oil of that, pressed out, one should drink with a decoction of harītakī (chebulic myrobalan).
notes: kaṣāya = decoction (glossary). Completes the sentence of 129. 'tat-tailam' = oil from that mixture. Enrichment: tailam without qualifier is usually sesame oil (probable); here it is the oil pressed out from the tila mixture of 129.

words.gloss: in atasī (Linum usitatissimum, flax), sarṣapa (Brassica spp., mustard), eraṇḍa (Ricinus communis, castor) and karañja (Pongamia pinnata, pongam tree) (all standard; species of sarṣapa varies)

hindi: अतसी यानी अलसी, सर्षप यानी सरसों, एरण्ड यानी अरण्डी और करञ्ज यानी करंज में भी यही विधि है।
english: This procedure holds also for atasī (flax), sarṣapa (mustard), eraṇḍa (castor) and karañja (pongam tree).

text_flags.why: stray anusvāra after ai (sarṣapa + eraṇḍa = sarṣapairaṇḍa), and apyaṃ is apyayaṃ with ya dropped (restores 16 syllables)

notes: The four names are kept in the translation; identifications are in the word gloss (karañja is Pongamia pinnata in the standard reading; a Caesalpinia species is sometimes proposed).

words.gloss: firm and thick, like the tooth of dantī
born of dantī (Baliospermum montanum, wild croton; probable) and dravantī (disputed)

hindi: दन्ती यानी जंगली जमालगोटा और द्रवन्ती से उत्पन्न मूल, जो दन्ती के दाँत के समान दृढ़ और स्थूल हो।
english: The root born of dantī and dravantī, firm and thick like the tooth of dantī.
notes: Unsure whether dantī-danta is 'tooth/tusk of dantī' or 'dantī (the drug) tooth-like'; the simile 'like' is also an interpretation of the compound. dantī could also point to an elephant (dantin); not decided. Low confidence.

words.gloss: vikāṣin (loosening the bonds of the tissues; see 125)

hindi: कुछ ताँबे जैसा लाल और श्याव, तीक्ष्ण, उष्ण, शीघ्र करने वाला और विकाषी।
english: Slightly coppery-red and dusky, sharp, hot, quick-acting, and vikāṣin.

text_flags.why: possible: ṣ for ś; the technical word is vikāśin/vikāsin

notes: Describes the root of 132. āśukārin = literally 'doing quickly'. vikāṣin left as a technical term.

hindi: भारी, वात को कुपित करने वाला, पित्त और कफ को पिघलाने वाला।
english: Heavy, provoking Vāta, dissolving Pitta and Kapha.
notes: Still describes the root. 'vilāyana' is literally melting/dissolving; 'prakopin' literally 'provoking'. Both are the text's statements.

words.gloss: smeared with honey (kṣaudra) and pippalī (Piper longum, long pepper; standard)
within clay and kuśa (kuśa grass, Desmostachya bipinnata; standard)

hindi: उसे शहद और पिप्पली यानी पीपर से लिप्त करके मिट्टी और कुश के बीच स्वेदित करे।
english: One should steam that, smeared with honey and pippalī (long pepper), between clay and kuśa (sacred grass).
notes: svedayet is literally 'cause to sweat'; 'steam' is the plain sense. mṛt-kuśa-antare: 'in the space between clay and kuśa' (kuśa kept as a name); the method is not described further.

hindi: धूप में सुखाए; क्योंकि इसकी विकाषिता नष्ट हो जाती है।
english: One should dry it in the sunshine ... for its vikāṣitā is destroyed.

text_flags.why: damaged: 'myarkau gives 17 syllables for 16 and has no clear sense (perhaps 'tyarke or similar)
possible: hato (m. nom.) and vikāṣitāṃ (acc.) do not agree; perhaps hanti / hataḥ with a different subject

notes: The text is damaged. The translation is tentative: only 'dry in the sunshine' and 'its vikāṣitā is destroyed' are read; the damaged part 'myarkau is left out of the translation. Low confidence. The printed hato (m. nom.) and vikāṣitāṃ (acc.) do not agree; 'its vikāṣitā is destroyed' rests on the possible emendation hatā ... vikāṣitā and is only a tentative reading. The printed line scans 16 syllables.

words.gloss: with mastu (curd whey), madirā (spirituous drink), takra (buttermilk), pīlu (Salvadora persica; standard) juice and āsava (fermented drink)

hindi: उसे मस्तु यानी दही का पानी, मदिरा, तक्र यानी मट्ठा, पीलु के रस और आसव यानी खमीर उठाए हुए पेय के साथ पिए।
english: One should drink that with mastu (curd whey), madirā (spirituous drink), takra (buttermilk), pīlu juice and āsava (fermented drink).
notes: 'pīlurasa' read as 'juice of pīlu' (pīlu a drug name); it could also be read as a separate rasa. tat = the dried root of 132-136.

words.gloss: one whose body is abhiṣyanna (oozing, saturated)
one having prameha (group of urinary disorders, including diabetes-type madhumeha)

hindi: जिसका शरीर अभिष्यन्न हो, गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ वाला, प्रमेह यानी मूत्र-विकारों वाला, जठर वाला, गर यानी कृत्रिम विष वाला,
english: A person whose body is abhiṣyanna, one with gulma (abdominal lump), with prameha (urinary disorders), with jaṭhara (belly disease), with gara (compound poison),
notes: GROUPING: 138-141 form one sentence (a list of persons, then the preparation). abhiṣyanna is left as a technical word, literally 'flowed forth, oozing'. The four terms are disease names kept in the translation: gulma = abdominal lump; prameha = the group of urinary disorders (madhumeha, diabetes-type, is one kind); jaṭhara = belly disease (udara-type, ascites-like); gara = compound poison (standard readings).

words.gloss: with juices of cow, deer and goat
one having worms in the bowel (koṣṭha)

hindi: गो, मृग और अज के रसों से; पाण्डु वर्ण वाला, कोष्ठ में कृमि वाला, भगन्दर यानी गुदा के पास के नासूर वाला,
english: With the juices of cow, deer and goat; a person who is pale, who has worms in the bowel, who has bhagandara (anal fistula),
notes: 'rasa' may mean meat-juice or broth; kept as 'juice'. It probably belongs with siddham of 140 (cooked with those juices). pāṇḍukrimikoṣṭhī may also be one bahuvrīhi 'pale and with worms in the bowel'. Order of phrases kept as printed. Enrichment: in this list of persons pāṇḍu very probably names the disease pāṇḍu (pallor with anaemia-type illness); the translation keeps 'pale' (earlier sense decision). krimi-koṣṭha = worms in the bowel (intestinal worms). The animal juices (rasa) are probably meat juices of cow, deer and goat; translation keeps 'juices'.

words.gloss: with the decoction and paste of that
with juice of the daśamūla (the ten roots)

hindi: उसके काढ़े और कल्क से तथा दशमूल यानी दस जड़ों के समूह के रस से पकाया हुआ,
english: Cooked with the decoction and paste of that, and with the juice of the daśamūla,
notes: 'tat' = the root of 132-137. The thing cooked is ghṛta (ghee), named in 141 (or taila in 142). The ten roots are a named group; not listed here. Enrichment: daśamūla, the ten roots (standard group): bilva, agnimantha, śyonāka, pāṭalā, gambhārī (the larger five) and śāliparṇī, pṛśniparṇī, bṛhatī, kaṇṭakārī, gokṣura (the smaller five).

words.gloss: visarpa (spreading inflammatory skin disease, erysipelas-like; probable), vidradhi (deep abscess; standard), alajī (a skin disorder; unsure), kaṣā (unclear), and burning (dāha)

hindi: घृत विसर्प यानी फैलने वाले जलन-सूजन के त्वचा रोग, विद्रधि यानी गहरे फोड़े, अलजी, कषा और दाह को जीत ले।
english: The ghee may overcome visarpa (spreading inflammatory skin disease), vidradhi (deep abscess), alajī, kaṣā and burning.

text_flags.why: possible: kaṣā is not a known disorder word; kṣata (wound) is a guess; kaṣāya is another

notes: The ghṛta is the 'siddham' of 140. The disorder names are classical terms (visarpa and vidradhi are identified in the gloss; alajī and kaṣā stay unresolved); the word kaṣā is unclear. Low confidence.

words.gloss: gulma (abdominal lump), meha (urinary disorders), arśas (haemorrhoids, piles), vibandha (constipation), Kapha and wind

hindi: तैल तो गुल्म यानी पेट की गाँठ, मेह यानी मूत्र-विकार, अर्श यानी बवासीर, विबन्ध यानी मलावरोध, कफ और वायु को जीत ले।
english: Oil, on the other hand, [may overcome] gulma (abdominal lump), meha (urinary disorders), arśas (piles), binding (vibandha, constipation), Kapha and wind.
notes: The verb 'jayet' is carried over from 141 and supplied in translation. arśas = haemorrhoids (piles); meha = the prameha group of urinary disorders, of which diabetes-type madhumeha is one kind (standard). tailam unqualified is usually sesame oil (probable). vibandha = binding, obstruction.

words.gloss: obstruction of stool, semen and wind, and pains of wind

hindi: महास्नेह मल, शुक्र और वात की रुकावट तथा वायु की पीड़ाओं को जीत ले।
english: The mahāsneha [may overcome] obstruction of stool, semen and wind, and pains of wind.

text_flags.why: the sign '~' is a scan error for the class nasal ṅ

notes: The verb 'jayet' is supplied from 141. mahāsneha is kept literally ('great sneha'); its contents are not stated here. The compound could also read 'stool, semen, obstruction of Vāta, pains of wind'. Enrichment: in the standard usage mahāsneha means the four fats taken together (ghee, oil, muscle-fat vasā, marrow majjā), or a medicated preparation of them; which is meant here is not decided (probable). śukra = semen.

words.gloss: of bhṛṅgī (drug name; identity disputed, Eclipta prostrata or Clerodendrum serratum proposed)
combined with jaggery, honey and ghee

hindi: दन्ती के रस में अथवा भृङ्गी के रस में, गुड़, शहद और घृत से युक्त,
english: In the juice of dantī, or of bhṛṅgī, combined with jaggery, honey and ghee,
notes: 'dantyā rase' is correct sandhi for dantyāḥ rase. The subject (a lick, leha) comes in 145.

words.gloss: dispelling burning, heat and meha (urinary disorders incl. diabetes-type)

hindi: विरेचन के लिए पकाया हुआ लेह, दाह, सन्ताप और मेह यानी मूत्र-विकार को दूर करने वाला।
english: A cooked lick (leha), for the purpose of purging, dispelling burning, heat and meha.
notes: GROUPING: 144 and 145 are one sentence ('combined with ... , a cooked leha'). nut = pusher away, dispelling. virekārthe is a locative of purpose.

words.gloss: with ajagandhā (drug name; identity disputed, no identification adopted)

hindi: वात की तृष्णा में और पित्त के ज्वर यानी बुखार में वही अजगन्धा के साथ हो।
english: In Vāta-thirst and in Pitta fever, that very (leha) would be with ajagandhā.
notes: 'vātatarṣe jvare paitte' could also be read as 'in Vāta, in thirst, in fever of the Pitta kind'. 'would be with ajagandhā' means the same leha is made with ajagandhā; kept literal. ajagandhā is literally 'goat-smell'; kept as a drug name.

words.gloss: in the juice of dhātrī (= āmalakī, Phyllanthus emblica, Indian gooseberry; standard)

hindi: तब दन्ती और द्रवन्ती की जड़ों को धात्री यानी आँवले के रस में पकाए।
english: One should then cook the roots of dantī and dravantī in the juice of dhātrī (Indian gooseberry).
notes: 'dhātrī' is a drug name (literally 'nurse'); standard synonym of āmalakī, Indian gooseberry (Phyllanthus emblica); standard.

hindi: तीन भाग, और फाणित के दो भाग, तेल अथवा घी में प्रयोग करे।
english: One should employ three portions, and two of phāṇita, in oil or in ghee.

text_flags.why: possible: dh for dv ('dvau' two); the printed dhau gives no sense

notes: The sense is uncertain: the construction 'three portions, and two from phāṇita' and the meaning of bhajet (employ / add / fry) are doubtful. Low confidence. phāṇitāt is ablative as printed; 'two of phāṇita' is a loose guess at the construction.
